The last driver whose vehicle is still operational is awarded the victory. Demolition derbies originated in the United States and quickly spread to other Western nations. For example, Australia's first demolition derby took place in January 1963. In the UK and parts of Europe, demolition derbies (sometimes called destruction derbies) are often held at the end of a full day of banger racing.

description_text:
The 2015 Hyundai Tucson serves up a satisfying blend of fashion, features and maneuverability, but other rival small crossovers can do that, while providing superior versatility and a more enjoyable driving experience.
Vehicle overviewCapable of being comfortable, spacious and economical, crossover SUVs are some of the most popular family automobiles on the road today. Practically every automaker has answered the call for these versatile vehicles, and as a result there are lots of impressive crossovers from which to choose. Hyundai's 2015 Tucson is a compact crossover that is certainly likable for its maneuverable dimensions and stylish exterior, but up against plenty of excellent competition, it seems to need more to stand out.
This spritely Hyundai isn't without virtue, but there are several things holding it back from being a top choice. The 2015 Tucson eases over small bumps and highway imperfections while also being easy to maneuver in to parking spots, but it doesn't fare so well if you're trying to pack all the family gear for vacation. Passenger space is adequate, but the Tucson has less cargo space than pretty much all of the segment leaders. The smallish footprint of the Tucson seems to be paired with a similarly underpowered base engine, too. Decent performance can be had with the optional 2.4-liter engine, but there are much more inspiring options out there.
With a smaller-than-average footprint and less powerful engines, you'd think the Tucson would do well on fuel economy -- and for the most part, it does. During Edmunds testing, we found the Tucson's EPA-estimated 24 mpg combined an easy number to achieve. Most rivals, though, can offer better mileage numbers to start with, and the best rivals return numbers as high as 30 mpg combined.
As previously mentioned, there's quite a bit of selection in the crossover segment these days. The excellent 2015 Mazda CX-5 is one of the sleekest crossovers available, and it's one of our favorites to drive. Where the Tucson is uninspired and rather dull to drive, the CX-5 is responsive and fun and has a particularly upscale interior. The Honda CR-V and the 2015 Ford Escape are two of the most well-rounded vehicles in the segment, thanks to quiet, upscale interiors and laudable fuel economy ratings. The CR-V and the Escape also have more cargo capacity than the Tucson. A closer match for the Tucson in terms of size is the 2015 Jeep Cherokee, but even the Cherokee is laid out in a way that the backseat offers more passenger space.
Compared to such strong competition, the Edmunds C rated 2015 Hyundai Tucson is a passable choice, but its rivals are a bit harder to resist.
2015 Hyundai Tucson models
The 2015 Hyundai Tucson is a five-passenger compact crossover SUV offered in three trim levels: GLS, SE and Limited.
The base GLS comes standard with the 2.0-liter four-cylinder engine, 17-inch alloy wheels, privacy glass, LED running lights, a rear spoiler, cloth upholstery, air-conditioning, full power accessories, a trip computer, a height-adjustable driver seat, 60/40-split-folding rear seatbacks with recline, Bluetooth phone and audio connectivity, a tilt-and-telescoping steering wheel and a six-speaker sound system with a CD player, iPod/USB connectivity and satellite radio.
Available as an optional extra on the GLS is the Popular Equipment package, which includes automatic headlights, a 4.3-inch touchscreen display, a rearview camera, a six-way power driver seat (with two-way power lumbar) and cloth/premium vinyl (leatherette) upholstery.
The SE gets all of the above equipment, along with the bigger 2.4-liter engine, foglights, heated side mirrors, sport body cladding, roof rails, heated front seats and rear climate vents.
Step up to the Limited and you'll get 18-inch wheels, chrome exterior trim, keyless ignition and entry, leather upholstery, dual-zone automatic climate control, an auto-dimming rearview mirror, Hyundai's Blue Link telematics and a retractable rear cargo cover.
Optional for the Limited is the Technology package, which adds LED taillights, a panoramic sunroof, an upgraded seven-speaker sound system, a 7-inch touchscreen, HD radio and a navigation system.

description_text:
The Aspark Owl (Japanese: アスパーク OWL) is an all-electric battery-powered sports car manufactured by Japanese engineering firm Aspark (アスパーク), under development since 2018, with the goal of making the fastest accelerating electric car. It will be built by Manifattura Automobili Torino (MAT) in Italy. Aspark plans a production run of 50 vehicles, with a list price of €2.5 million. The OWL was publicly unveiled in concept form at the 2017 Frankfurt Auto Show, and the production version was unveiled in November 2019 at the Dubai International Motor Show.\
The OWL has carbon fibre body work built around a carbon fibre monocoque chassis weighing 120 kg (265 lb). A stainless steel support structure is incorporated in the roof to increase the bodywork's strength. Changes to the bodywork from the concept include the addition of wing mirrors, an active rear wing and a redesigned rear glass. The car features double wishbone suspension with hydraulic dampers and torque vectoring for improved handling. Stopping power is handled by a carbon-ceramic braking system with 10-piston front calipers and 4-piston rear calipers.[6]
It has been claimed that the OWL can accelerate from 0-97 km/h (60 mph) in 1.69 seconds, 0-100 km/h (62 mph) in 1.9 seconds, 0-299 km/h (186 mph) in 10.6 seconds, and can attain a top speed of 400 km/h (249 mph), which would make it the fastest accelerating production car in the world.[7] However, at least some of these claims are most likely unrealistic, due to the physical limits of automobile acceleration imposed by the friction of tires with the road, and a lack of convincing video evidence.

Engine and transmission
The 5.0-litre twin-turbo V8 engineThe Agera is powered by an in-house developed 5.0-litre V8 engine and fitted with twin-turbochargers which generates a maximum power output of 706 kW (960 PS; 947 hp) at 6,900 rpm and 1,100 N⋅m (811 lbf⋅ft) of torque at 4,000 rpm.[9] The total weight of the engine is only 197 kg (434 lb) due to a carbon fibre inlet manifold and aluminium construction. The transmission is a specially developed 7-speed dual-clutch with paddle shifters. It is the first dual-clutch transmission to feature only one input shaft. The second clutch slows down the input shaft during up shifts in order to reduce the time it takes to synchronise the next gear, resulting in faster shift times. Most notably, the transmission weighs only 81 kg (179 lb).[10]

Exterior and interior
Koenigsegg Agera
Koenigsegg Agera R InteriorThe Agera has a body made from impregnated carbon fibre/kevlar with lightweight reinforcements. The car's hardtop roof is stowable under the front hood lid. The chassis is also made out of carbon fibre with an aluminium honeycomb structure that comes with integrated fuel tanks for optimal weight distribution and safety. The rear wing is electronically adjustable with auto setting or manual control in order to have as little compromise as possible between low drag and downforce, depending on driving conditions.[12] The Agera comes with forged aluminum wheels with centre locking nuts, measuring 19-inch on the front and 20-inch on the rear and wrapped in a set of Michelin Super Sport tyres that can be used for speeds of up to 420 km/h (260 mph). Other notable features include the trademark dihedral-synchro-helix-actuation doors, a new traction control system, LED lighting, blue hood stripes that continue through the cockpit of the car and a custom interior with a new Ghost light lighting system, which uses carbon nanotubes in a unique configuration to shine through the car's aluminium buttons.[13]

description_text:
Dice (singular die or dice) are small, throwable objects with marked sides that can rest in multiple positions. They are used for generating random values, commonly as part of tabletop games, including dice games, board games, role-playing games, and games of chance.
A traditional die is a cube with each of its six faces marked with a different number of dots (pips) from one to six. When thrown or rolled, the die comes to rest showing a random integer from one to six on its upper surface, with each value being equally likely. Dice may also have polyhedral or irregular shapes, may have faces marked with numerals or symbols instead of pips and may have their numbers carved out from the material of the dice instead of marked on it. Loaded dice are designed to favor some results over others for cheating or entertainment.

Low poly cars are commonly used in 3D worlds such as video games, simulations, and architectural visualizations. They are popular in these contexts because they can be easily rendered in real-time, allowing for smooth and seamless interactions with the environment.
In video games, low poly cars are often used as props or vehicles that the player can interact with. Low poly cars can also be used to populate the game world, providing a sense of realism and scale to the environment.
In simulations, low poly cars are often used to represent vehicles in traffic or as part of a larger scene. They can be animated and manipulated to simulate real-world scenarios, allowing users to explore and interact with different scenarios in a controlled environment.
In architectural visualizations, low poly cars are used to provide a sense of scale and context to the design. They can be placed in parking lots or on streets to show how the building or structure fits into the surrounding environment. Because low poly cars are easy to manipulate and render, they can be a valuable tool for architects and designers to communicate their vision to clients and stakeholders.
Overall, low poly cars are a versatile and useful asset in the 3D world, providing a way to add visual interest, context, and realism to a variety of different applications.

description_text:
The RAR file contains:
1.) 3 Blender files:
LONGBOARD - a blender file with the board model (709360 vertices). The model consists of 7 parts: board (1), trucks (2),  wheels(4). There are 24 different looks of the board (6 types of the deck material - light/dark, light/dark with the Ballon, light/dark with the Umbrella Cat) and 4 wheel colors (black, orange, pink, blue). All the textures are packed into the blender file and they also exist separately in a folder in the RAR file. There are 2K and 4K textures available.
LONGBOARD_PROCEDURAL_MATERIALS - a blender file with the board model with procedural material (light deck wood with no image, pink wheels) - you can make your own drawing and adjust the colors as you wish :) 
LONGBOARD_RIGGED - a blender file with the rigged board. The rig allows to move and rotate the board, rotate the trucks, tilt the board, rotate the wheels. You can rotate the board around the center pivot and around the front and back truck. However, there is a rig limitation concerning the rotation around one of the 3 rotation axis (you can see it in the youtube clip).
2.) Baked Texures:LONGBOARD_2K/LONGBOARD_2K - textures for the material setup (BOARD-6 diffuse maps, 1 normal map; TRUCKS- diffuse, metallic, normal, roughness map; WHEELS- 4 diffuse maps, normal and roughness)UV - the folder contains png pictures with a default UV mapping (for wheels, trucks and the deck sparately)
3.) OBJ and FBX file (only model, no materials)
4.) 2 MP4 clips regarding the material setup and the rig (YT clip)

description_text:
The UEFA Champions League (abbreviated as UCL, or sometimes, UEFA CL) is an annual club association football competition organised by the Union of European Football Associations (UEFA) and contested by top-division European clubs, deciding the competition winners through a round robin group stage to qualify for a double-legged knockout format, and a single leg final. It is the most-watched club competition in the world and the third most-watched football competition overall, behind only the UEFA European Championship and the FIFA World Cup. It is one of the most prestigious football tournaments in the world and the most prestigious club competition in European football, played by the national league champions (and, for some nations, one or more runners-up) of their national associations.
Introduced in 1955 as the Coupe des Clubs Champions Européens (French for European Champion Clubs' Cup), and commonly known as the European Cup, it was initially a straight knockout tournament open only to the champions of Europe's domestic leagues, with its winner reckoned as the European club champion. The competition took on its current name in 1992, adding a round-robin group stage in 1991 and allowing multiple entrants from certain countries since the 1997–98 season.[1] It has since been expanded, and while most of Europe's national leagues can still only enter their champion, the strongest leagues now provide up to four teams.[2][3] Clubs that finish next-in-line in their national league, having not qualified for the Champions League, are eligible for the second-tier UEFA Europa League competition, and since 2021, for the third-tier UEFA Europa Conference League.[4]
In its present format, the Champions League begins in late June with a preliminary round, three qualifying rounds and a play-off round, all played over two legs. The six surviving teams enter the group stage, joining 26 teams qualified in advance. The 32 teams are drawn into eight groups of four teams and play each other in a double round-robin system. The eight group winners and eight runners-up proceed to the knockout phase that culminates with the final match in late May or early June.[5] The winner of the Champions League qualifies for the following year's Champions League, the UEFA Super Cup, and the FIFA Club World Cup.[6][7]
Spanish clubs have the highest number of victories (19 wins), followed by England (15 wins) and Italy (12 wins). England has the largest number of winning teams, with six clubs having won the title. The competition has been won by 23 clubs, 13 of which have won it more than once, and eight successfully defended their title.[8] Real Madrid is the most successful club in the tournament's history, having won it 14 times, including the first five seasons and also five of the last ten.[9] Only one club has won all of their matches in a single tournament en route to the tournament victory: Bayern Munich in the 2019–20 season.[10]
Only two teams in the history of the competition have won the tournament playing the final in their home ground: Real Madrid at the Santiago Bernabéu in 1957 and Inter Milan at the San Siro in 1965.
Milan in 1964 was the first city that had two teams that had won the competition at least once, and after 59 years in 2023, Manchester also earned this title; in years other cities came close to claim this title as well, but their teams lost the finals like Madrid with Atletico Madrid in three occasions, London with Arsenal and Tottenham and Belgrade with Partizan.
Manchester City are the current European champions, having beaten Inter Milan 1–0 in the 2023 final for their first title.

description_text:
A simple, stylized, game-ready asset inspired by the collectible gems in old games like Spyro the Dragon and Crash Bandicoot, made in Blender with 9 colors for the gems. Theoretically all colors if you edit that part yourself, but still 9 if you don't. There are probably other ways to package the textures, but I'm hoping this is simpler for the end user.
792 vertices, 740 faces, and 1100 tris per ball. 10 spikes, 20 gem faces. As with most things, lighting makes a big difference in showing off their shine, compare Group Previews 1 and 2 for a demonstration. Does not break apart into individual gemstones, nor do the spikes fly outward like shrapnel.
File types include .fbx (and necessary textures), .stl, .blend, .mtl, and .obj. for each color. You probably could 3D print it, but it might not be a good idea.
I've been calling them Greed Urchins during the development process because they're spiky, shiny balls of gold and gemstones, like sea urchins devised by an insanely rich person. Usable for any purpose that strikes your fancy, including but not limited to:
-Collectible Treasures
-Magical Landmines
-Fantasy Lighting Fixtures (if put on the end of a chain or a stick, which should also work for weapons)
-Projectiles
-Decoration
-Artifacts of Power
-A Spinning Icon for Loading Screens
-Power-ups
-Soul Jars
-Impractically Expensive Electrical Conductors
-Flying Drone Enemies
-Caltrops Used By The World's Flashiest Ninja
-Floating Grapple Points
-Dwarven Disco Ball
-Worn Jewelry for Masochists
-Fixed Points In A Laser Security Grid
-Elemental Fuel Tanks
-The Ball In A Sport That Doesn't Exist
and more that I can't think of at the moment!

description_text:
Hi there, this is a high poly 3D model of a Toyota MR2 SW20 Rev. 2 (1993) that was created using subdivision surfaces in Blender. It’s my first finished car model and the interior proportions aren’t the most accurate, so I decided to share this model for free. It also serves as a preview of my modeling skills for those who are interested in buying my paid models.
I used Blender’s shrinkwrap method to model most of the car body (which I will avoid in future works), resulting in the subdivision surface modifier having to be applied destructively to those objects. The objects that do not use shrinkwrap are base meshes that can be subdivided as viewport modifiers or within the renderer. Included is a readme listing which objects you should/should not subdivide as well as some other helpful info.
For Blender 3.6.5+ users, a .blend file is included with textures, materials, and subdivision surface modifiers already added to the model, so it's ready to render in Cycles.
Enjoy!

description_text:
I crated this Dice Model in Blender.
Dice are small, throwable objects with marked sides that can rest in multiple positions. They are used for generating random values, commonly as part of tabletop games, including dice games, board games, role-playing games, and games of chance.
A traditional die is a cube with each of its six faces marked with a different number of dots (pips) from one to six. When thrown or rolled, the die comes to rest showing a random integer from one to six on its upper surface, with each value being equally likely. Dice may also have polyhedral or irregular shapes, may have faces marked with numerals or symbols instead of pips and may have their numbers carved out from the material of the dice instead of marked on it. Loaded dice are designed to favor some results over others for cheating or entertainment.

The Big Gold Belt is a historic professional wrestling championship belt that has represented multiple world championships throughout its history.
Originally designed in 1985 by silversmith Charles Crumrine and commissioned by Jim Crockett Promotions for NWA World Heavyweight Champion Ric Flair, the championship belt has three large gold plates with a distinctive name plate onto which the champion's name was etched. The original championship belt design was known for being unbranded as it only read World Heavyweight Wrestling Champion and bore no initials or trademark of its owning promotion.

In a time when personal vehicles are no longer the norm and most means of transportation have both been automated and taken airborne, causing the streets and old highways being left empty and unused… There are still those who have an affinity to the aesthetics and technology from the turn of the millennium. description_text:
Gloss black 1975 Porsche 911 (930) Turbo, high-poly, rigged and animated. Ready for close-up renders, animation and real-time use.
GEOMETRY

  - 932,874 polygons / 966,345 vertices

  - Mostly quads, smooth subdivided bodywork

  - 73 separate parts (body, glass, chrome, lights, wheels, interior details)

MATERIALS AND TEXTURES

  - PBR materials: clear-coat black paint, chrome, glass, rubber, lights, plates

  - 24 textures up to 4K (base colour, normal, ORM), UVs kept

RIG AND ANIMATION

  - Armature with Root, Body, Steering and 4 Wheel bones

  - Wheel spin driven automatically by a distance control, so wheels roll at the correct speed

  - Front steering driven by a single steer control

  - Body roll and pitch for cornering and braking

  - Includes a 9-second drive animation (pull away, S-bend, braking, steering sweep)

FILE FORMATS

  - Blender 5.2 (.blend): static and rigged versions, Cycles studio lighting, cameras and floor included

  - FBX: rigged, with baked animation

  - glTF / GLB

  - OBJ + MTL with textures

  - USDZ

  - Alembic (.abc) of the drive animation

  - Separate textures folder

NOTES

  - Best materials in .blend and .glb; OBJ and FBX carry simplified materials

  - Not real-world scale (about 10% oversized)

  - Editorial use: Porsche is a registered trademark

CREDITSBased on FREE 1975 Porsche 911 (930) Turbo by Lionsharp Studios ), licensed CC BY 4.0 (creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/).Modified by Steve: gloss black paint, geometry subdivided ~4x (241k to 933k polygons), rigging, drive animation, new studio lighting, and export to additional formats.

description_text:
A detailed mechanical front axle for a modern compact sports car, modelled part by part like the real assembly: every bolt goes through its holes, the struts clamp into the knuckles, the calipers bolt to their brackets, the discs sit on the hubs and the wheels on their studs. Each part is a separate object, so the kit can be shown assembled, exploded, or used piece by piece.Built for automotive visualisation, technical and training illustrations, product shots, cutaways and close-up renders.
Contents (98 parts)

  - Two complete corners (left and right): wheel, brakes, hub, knuckle, strut, lower arm, ball joint, steering linkage and driveshaft on each side.

  - Wheels: 18-inch multi-spoke alloy rims with a diamond-cut face, 235/40 R18 tyres with tread and moulded sidewall lettering, lug nuts and 5 wheel studs.

  - Brakes: two-piece drilled and vented floating discs with a black anodised hat, red multi-piston fixed calipers with pads and pistons, billet caliper brackets, braided brake hoses, dust shields, ABS sensors and cables.

  - Hubs: hub flanges with bearing units, hub bolts and axle bolts.

  - Suspension: adjustable coilover struts (red springs, anodised collars, threaded sleeves, top mounts, bump stops, chrome rods), cast knuckles, cast aluminium lower arms with bushes, bolted ball joints with boots.

  - Steering: tie rods with tie-rod ends, electric steering rack with bellows and heat shield.

  - Driveline: left and right driveshafts with CV joints and boots.

  - Chassis: cast aluminium front subframe with braces and mounting bolts, front anti-roll bar with bushes and clamps, adjustable drop links, ride-height sensor.

  - Fasteners: every bolt, nut and stud modelled with real threads.

  - 98 objects, 2,510,852 triangles (1,618,274 faces), 1,256,540 vertices in total.

  - Quads and triangles only, no n-gons, closed manifold shells, no duplicate vertices, clean normals.

  - Non-overlapping UVs on every part, no stretching, even texel density within each texture set.

  - Real-world scale in metres, transforms applied, the assembly sits on its tyres at Z = 0; overall 1.77 x 0.82 x 0.98 m.

  - Named parts grouped by system; all parts separate and ready to move.

Textures (PNG)

  - BaseColor, Roughness, Metalness, AO and Normal maps (OpenGL and DirectX) for every set.

  - Real finishes: raw cast iron, cast and machined aluminium, turned disc faces, gloss caliper paint, powder-coated springs, anodised parts, clear and yellow zinc plating, hard chrome, rubber, polyurethane.

  - New-part look, authored from the models themselves, no scans.

Formats

Notes

description_text:
Highly detailed Rigged 3D model of the Toyota Supra A90 (basic interior included), meticulously crafted to maintain exact real-world proportions and clean mesh/material organization. Produced by Anatolian Studios, this model is designed to be instantly ready for your renders, animations, or visualization projects without requiring any redesign, scaling, or adjustments.
Key Features:

  - 
Built to Real-World Scale: Modeled accurately in meters with exact physical proportions — no rescaling needed.

  - 
Detailed Exterior & Basic Interior: Fully detailed body, cabin, and trim, suitable for both close-up hero shots and animation.

  - 
Clean, Organized Structure: Every body panel, wheel, light, and trim piece is a separate, logically named object, grouped under Chassis / Exterior / Glass / Interior / Lights / Wheels, with materials named to match their parts for a fast, professional workflow.

  - 
Easy-to-Edit Materials: Clean Principled BSDF setup using solid-color materials, no advanced texturing or node knowledge required.

  - 
Correct Glass Setup: Transparent and glass surfaces are properly configured and export-friendly across all included formats.

  - 
Scene Ready: Centered at origin (0,0,0) with reset transforms and a single master parent, so the entire vehicle can be moved, rotated, or scaled as one unit.

Vehicle Rig (included):
The .blend file includes a production-ready vehicle rig, no add-ons needed. 
One slider steers both front wheels and the steering wheel together; drive the car forward and all four wheels roll automatically at the correct rate. Also included: per-axle and per-wheel manual spin, independent suspension travel on all four corners, and body pitch/roll for braking dive and cornering lean. Bones are cleanly named (CTRL_Root, CTRL_Body, CTRL_Wheel_FL/FR/RL/RR) with pivots centered on each axle, and the model is skinned so the skeleton carries over to the FBX and glTF files.
Documented rig guide (pdf) is included in the files.
Included File Formats:

  - 
.blend (Native Blender file — full rig with automatic steering and wheel roll, materials assigned, rendered in Cycles/Eevee)

  - 
.fbx (Widely supported format, retains geometry and material data)

  - 
.fbx (rigged) (Same model with bones and skinning included)

  - 
.obj & .mtl (Universal 3D format)

  - 
.gltf / .glb (Optimized format for real-time engines, web viewing, and AR/VR)

  - 
.glb (rigged) (Same model with bones and skinning included)

  - 
.usdz / .usdc (Universal Scene Description — AR Quick Look, iOS, and USD pipelines)

Technical Specifications:

  - 
Polygons: 200000

  - 
Vertices: 190000

  - 
Geometry: Quads

  - 
Textures: No

  - 
Materials: Yes

  - 
UV Mapped: Mixed

  - 
Rigged: Yes (.blend, .fbx, .glb)

Please Note:

  - The rigged and un-rigged versions are supplied as separate files. The standard .fbx / .glb / .obj / .usdz files contain no skeleton and keep the full group hierarchy intact; the files marked rigged contain the bones and skinning.

  - The rig's automatic steering and wheel roll are expression-driven and run in Blender. In FBX and glTF the bones, skinning and wheel pivots are fully present and can be posed or animated, but that automation does not transfer — a limitation of the interchange formats, not of the model.

Disclaimer: This is an unofficial, fan-made model created for visualization purposes and is not affiliated with or endorsed by the manufacturer. All brand names, logos, and trademarks are property of their respective owners.

A generic MMA arena on event night, empty and ready for the next bout, built in a clean low poly style with flat shading. The 18.5 x 14.3 m floor of dark sealed concrete has two graphite block walls, 5 m high, in an L and no ceiling. Every model is a single mesh at real-world scale in meters, with its origin at the base, 3 LODs, convex colliders and its own small palette texture, ready to drop into your sports or event game, arena level, diorama or VR scene. description_text: A low poly neighbourhood gym interior for game engines: a 10 x 7 m room, 3.2 m high, open on one side. Two treadmills, two spin bikes and a rower face the windows. A power rack with barbell stands on an oak platform beside an adjustable bench and leg press. A dumbbell rack, kettlebell set and GO HARD sign line the mirror wall under a lime LED strip. description_text:
This asset is a volumetric model of a Pagani Huayra AMG V12  in Gaussian Splatting PLY format. The Pagani Huayra primarily utilizes a hand-built 6.0-liter (5,980 cc) twin-turbo V12 engine, developed specifically for this model by the Mercedes-AMG division.Model Specifications:Format: PLY 3DGS Standard | Gaussians: ∼4.5M | Size: ∼71,69 MB
3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) is a next-generation Radiance Field. Unlike a traditional mesh, the scene is composed of anisotropic Gaussians with Spherical Harmonics. It allows real-world captures with reflections and transparencies and instant visualization. It delivers realistic, detailed scenes with fast rendering, which is why it is used in architecture, video games, virtual reality, simulation, and real-world environment reconstruction.
EXTRA COMPATIBILITY: V-Ray (in 3ds Max / other DCCs): Starting from recent versions like V-Ray 7, it natively supports loading and rendering Gaussian Splat files integrated with ray tracing. SuperSplat, PlayCanvas, Unity, Unreal Engine, SplatViz, Three.js, Blender, Babylon.js , among others.
For a quick preview, go to https://superspl.at/editor

description_text:
35-Car Rigacar-Ready Collection
A collection of 35 vehicle models, pre-prepared for fast, professional rigging with the free Rigacar addon for Blender.
Requirements
Blender 4.0 or newer (tested up to Blender 5.0+)The Rigacar addon installed and enabled (free, available on GitHub)Basic familiarity with the Append workflow
What's IncludedEach of the 35 cars comes with:
A clean, separated mesh: body, four wheels, and four brake discs as individual objectsCorrect Rigacar naming convention pre-applied:cars-bodycars-Wheel.Ft.L, cars-Wheel.Ft.R, cars-Wheel.Bk.L, cars-Wheel.Bk.Rcars-WheelBrake.Ft.L, cars-WheelBrake.Ft.R, cars-WheelBrake.Bk.L, cars-WheelBrake.Bk.RRealistic materials and shading (Cycles-tested)Organized outliner hierarchy for easy navigation
How to Use
Open your project in Blender.Go to File > Append, then navigate to the downloaded .blend file.Select the Collection for the car you want, and append it into your scene.With the car's objects selected, run Rigacar's Generate Rig operator (Rigacar detects the cars- naming automatically).Your car now has a working rig with steering, wheel rotation, and suspension — ready to animate.
Tips
Keep the naming convention intact if you duplicate or rename objects, or Rigacar won't recognize them.Each car is a separate collection, so you can append only the vehicles you need without importing the whole file.Materials use standard Principled BSDF nodes and can be freely edited or replaced.
SupportIf you run into any issues appending or rigging a car, reach out via the product page — happy to help troubleshoot.

description_text:
This Ice Hockey Goalie Guarding Pose is a high end, photorealistic 3D model, that will help you to add realism to your project. The model is suitable for any visual production - broadcast, high-res film close-ups, advertising, games, design visualisation, forensic presentation, etc. 
The model was initially created in 3Ds Max 2012, then fully textured and rendered using V-Ray. 
All geometry and visual aspects of the model are optimised to give you the highest possible quality for up to 2k renders. There is no post-production used on any of the renders you see. 
Features: 
-This model is accurately sized to match the real object.     -Objects are grouped and named according to their real purpose, allowing the model to be rigged and animated smoothly.     -Clean and optimised topology is used for maximum polygon efficiency.     -Model is fully sub-dividable to allow Turbosmooth Iterations to increase mesh smoothness if needed.     -All textures and materials are tailored and applied for high-quality render results.     -All objects have fully unwrapped UVs.     -No extra plugins are required for this model.     -Lights and cameras are not included in the scenes. 
Technical Specifications: 
-Model is included in 4 file formats.         -3ds Max V-Ray         -3ds Max Mental ray         -Cinema 4D R17 V-Ray         -OBJ     -Model consists of 263385 Faces and 267410 Vertices.     -Model Dimensions: 183.7157cm x 121.1311cm x 125.5232cm     -Units in all formats: #centimeters     -All Textures are PNG format with the following resolutions:         - 4096 x 4096 px         - 8192 x 8192 px 
Additional Notes: 
This model was created for 85 hours form our Leading 3D artists to ensure you get the best quality model and save precious production time. 
Are you looking to purchase more than one of our products? If so, we might be able to create a collection of products with a discount just for you!
Please contact us through the support for any inquiries.

description_text:
Highly detailed Rigged 3D model of the Lexus LFA Sport Concept (basic interior included), meticulously crafted to maintain exact real-world proportions and clean mesh/material organization. Produced by Anatolian Studios, this model is designed to be instantly ready for your renders, animations, or visualization projects without requiring any redesign, scaling, or adjustments.
Key Features:

  - 
Built to Real-World Scale: Modeled accurately in meters with exact physical proportions — no rescaling needed.

  - 
Detailed Exterior & Basic Interior: Fully detailed body, cabin, and trim, suitable for both close-up hero shots and animation.

  - 
Clean, Organized Structure: Every body panel, wheel, light, and trim piece is a separate, logically named object, grouped under Chassis / Exterior / Glass / Interior / Lights / Wheels, with materials named to match their parts for a fast, professional workflow.

  - 
Easy-to-Edit Materials: Clean Principled BSDF setup using solid-color materials, no advanced texturing or node knowledge required.

  - 
Correct Glass Setup: Transparent and glass surfaces are properly configured and export-friendly across all included formats.

  - 
Scene Ready: Centered at origin (0,0,0) with reset transforms and a single master parent, so the entire vehicle can be moved, rotated, or scaled as one unit.

Vehicle Rig (included):
The .blend file includes a production-ready vehicle rig, no add-ons needed. 
One slider steers both front wheels and the steering wheel together; drive the car forward and all four wheels roll automatically at the correct rate. Also included: per-axle and per-wheel manual spin, independent suspension travel on all four corners, and body pitch/roll for braking dive and cornering lean. Bones are cleanly named (CTRL_Root, CTRL_Body, CTRL_Wheel_FL/FR/RL/RR) with pivots centered on each axle, and the model is skinned so the skeleton carries over to the FBX and glTF files.
Documented rig guide (pdf) is included in the files.
Included File Formats:

  - 
.blend (Native Blender file — full rig with automatic steering and wheel roll, materials assigned, rendered in Cycles/Eevee)

  - 
.fbx (Widely supported format, retains geometry and material data)

  - 
.fbx (rigged) (Same model with bones and skinning included)

  - 
.obj & .mtl (Universal 3D format)

  - 
.gltf / .glb (Optimized format for real-time engines, web viewing, and AR/VR)

  - 
.glb (rigged) (Same model with bones and skinning included)

  - 
.usdz / .usdc (Universal Scene Description — AR Quick Look, iOS, and USD pipelines)

Technical Specifications:

  - 
Polygons: 300000

  - 
Vertices: 310000

  - 
Geometry: Quads

  - 
Textures: No

  - 
Materials: Yes

  - 
UV Mapped: Mixed

  - 
Rigged: Yes (.blend, .fbx, .glb)

Please Note:

  - The rigged and un-rigged versions are supplied as separate files. The standard .fbx / .glb / .obj / .usdz files contain no skeleton and keep the full group hierarchy intact; the files marked rigged contain the bones and skinning.

  - The rig's automatic steering and wheel roll are expression-driven and run in Blender. In FBX and glTF the bones, skinning and wheel pivots are fully present and can be posed or animated, but that automation does not transfer — a limitation of the interchange formats, not of the model.

Disclaimer: This is an unofficial, fan-made model created for visualization purposes and is not affiliated with or endorsed by the manufacturer. All brand names, logos, and trademarks are property of their respective owners.

description_text:
Highly detailed Rigged 3D model of the Toyota 2000GT, meticulously crafted to maintain exact real-world proportions and clean mesh/material organization. Produced by Anatolian Studios, this model is designed to be instantly ready for your renders, animations, or visualization projects without requiring any redesign, scaling, or adjustments.
Key Features:

  - 
Built to Real-World Scale: Modeled accurately in meters with exact physical proportions — no rescaling needed.

  - 
Detailed Exterior & Interior: Fully detailed body, cabin, and trim, suitable for both close-up hero shots and animation.

  - 
Clean, Organized Structure: Every body panel, wheel, light, and trim piece is a separate, logically named object, grouped under Chassis / Exterior / Glass / Interior / Lights / Wheels, with materials named to match their parts for a fast, professional workflow.

  - 
Easy-to-Edit Materials: Clean Principled BSDF setup using solid-color materials, no advanced texturing or node knowledge required.

  - 
Correct Glass Setup: Transparent and glass surfaces are properly configured and export-friendly across all included formats.

  - 
Scene Ready: Centered at origin (0,0,0) with reset transforms and a single master parent, so the entire vehicle can be moved, rotated, or scaled as one unit.

Vehicle Rig (included):
The .blend file includes a production-ready vehicle rig, no add-ons needed. 
One slider steers both front wheels and the steering wheel together; drive the car forward and all four wheels roll automatically at the correct rate. Also included: per-axle and per-wheel manual spin, independent suspension travel on all four corners, and body pitch/roll for braking dive and cornering lean. Bones are cleanly named (CTRL_Root, CTRL_Body, CTRL_Wheel_FL/FR/RL/RR) with pivots centered on each axle, and the model is skinned so the skeleton carries over to the FBX and glTF files.
Documented rig guide (pdf) is included in the files.
Included File Formats:

  - 
.blend (Native Blender file — full rig with automatic steering and wheel roll, materials assigned, rendered in Cycles/Eevee)

  - 
.fbx (Widely supported format, retains geometry and material data)

  - 
.fbx (rigged) (Same model with bones and skinning included)

  - 
.obj & .mtl (Universal 3D format)

  - 
.gltf / .glb (Optimized format for real-time engines, web viewing, and AR/VR)

  - 
.glb (rigged) (Same model with bones and skinning included)

  - 
.usdz / .usdc (Universal Scene Description — AR Quick Look, iOS, and USD pipelines)

Technical Specifications:

  - 
Polygons: 330000

  - 
Vertices: 320000

  - 
Geometry: Quads

  - 
Textures: No

  - 
Materials: Yes

  - 
UV Mapped: Mixed

  - 
Rigged: Yes (.blend, .fbx, .glb)

Please Note:

  - The rigged and un-rigged versions are supplied as separate files. The standard .fbx / .glb / .obj / .usdz files contain no skeleton and keep the full group hierarchy intact; the files marked rigged contain the bones and skinning.

  - The rig's automatic steering and wheel roll are expression-driven and run in Blender. In FBX and glTF the bones, skinning and wheel pivots are fully present and can be posed or animated, but that automation does not transfer — a limitation of the interchange formats, not of the model.

A fictional 1990s GT1-style homologation supercar inspired by the extreme road-going specials created during the golden era of endurance racing.
Based on the same generic 80s–90s supercar platform, this version transforms the original design into a much more focused machine with a deep front splitter, enlarged cooling openings, vented front bodywork, widened aerodynamic side skirts, revised rear bodywork, aggressive diffuser and a large motorsport-style rear wing.
The design keeps the proportions and character of a production supercar while introducing the functional aerodynamic elements typical of road cars developed alongside GT1 racing programs.
Created as a generic, non-branded fictional design, making it suitable for games, renders, dioramas, racing scenes and other automotive projects.
Car Features:

  - 1990s GT1 homologation-inspired styling

  - Wide, low supercar proportions

  - Deep front splitter and enlarged air intakes

  - Vented front bodywork

  - Sculpted side skirts and cooling ducts

  - Large adjustable-style rear wing

  - Rear diffuser

  - Quad exhaust layout

  - Motorsport-inspired multi-piece wheels

  - Detailed exterior and interior

  - Fully fictional, non-branded vehicle design

3D model Features:

  - 47 objects

  - Predescribed materials

  - Mixed UV

  - Scene also included

  - Seperate body panels

  - Mode

Part of the same fictional supercar family as the 80s–90s Generic Supercar, Facelifted Generic Supercar, and Early 1990s Generic Supercar.
HDRI used:
https://polyhaven.com/a/qwantani_sunset
Texture for ground used:
https://polyhaven.com/a/aerial_asphalt_01

description_text:
No AI was used in the making of this model.
Light Skipper: Team Yellow
The Light Skipper Space Racer is the perfect model to use for Sci-Fi themed races. With their pod styled design, rigged landing gear and cockpit, custom rigged pilot models, this model will be all you need to fill out your race tracks.
The Light Skipper Space Racer: Team Yellow is a highly detailed and feature rich 3D model, along with a matching rigged pilot model. All assets were made within Blender, with the exception of the decal images which were made using Affinity.
Included with the .blend file are 2K and 4K texture options (the 2K textures are applied to the exported models by default), and separate decal images with a stencil for making custom designs. Also included is a file of exported OBJ, FBX, and Glb models.All details and specifications can be found in the included guide.
The full Light Skipper collection is available to buy on my page. This includes all 6 Light Skipper variants along with a custom Light Skipper. The custom Light Skipper file includes all optional accessories and features seen across the whole collection, with the intention of creating your own custom Light Skipper model. 
Key Features:

  - Fully Rigged Landing Gear

  - Fully Rigged Cockpit Door

  - Fully Rigged Cockpit Ladder

  - Fully Rigged Air Brakes

  - Fully Rigged Pilot Model

  - Procedural materials

  - Multiple Customisation Options

  - 2K & 4K Texture Options

  - Movable Driving Frame

  - Posable Wings

description_text:
Highly detailed Rigged 3D model of the Nissan 240SX (basic interior included), meticulously crafted to maintain exact real-world proportions and clean mesh/material organization. Produced by Anatolian Studios, this model is designed to be instantly ready for your renders, animations, or visualization projects without requiring any redesign, scaling, or adjustments.
Key Features:

  - 
Built to Real-World Scale: Modeled accurately in meters with exact physical proportions — no rescaling needed.

  - 
Detailed Exterior & Basic Interior: Fully detailed body, cabin, and trim, suitable for both close-up hero shots and animation.

  - 
Clean, Organized Structure: Every body panel, wheel, light, and trim piece is a separate, logically named object, grouped under Chassis / Exterior / Glass / Interior / Lights / Wheels, with materials named to match their parts for a fast, professional workflow.

  - 
Easy-to-Edit Materials: Clean Principled BSDF setup using solid-color materials, no advanced texturing or node knowledge required.

  - 
Correct Glass Setup: Transparent and glass surfaces are properly configured and export-friendly across all included formats.

  - 
Scene Ready: Centered at origin (0,0,0) with reset transforms and a single master parent, so the entire vehicle can be moved, rotated, or scaled as one unit.

Vehicle Rig (included):
The .blend file includes a production-ready vehicle rig, no add-ons needed. 
One slider steers both front wheels and the steering wheel together; drive the car forward and all four wheels roll automatically at the correct rate. Also included: per-axle and per-wheel manual spin, independent suspension travel on all four corners, and body pitch/roll for braking dive and cornering lean. description_text:
Le Tartarus est l’une des études de conception de la gamme Tachyon de RAESR, aux côtés du Xénomorphe, du Wolfsblood et du Celeri, réalisés par le fondateur de la marque, Eric Rice, utilisant Solidworks. Dans la mythologie grecque, « Tartare » signifie à la fois une divinité et le lieu le plus bas des Enfers.
Dans les publications Instagram de la marque du 4 novembre 2022, on présentait quatre versions du Tachyon « Tartarus », ainsi que des détails sur la voiture — y compris sa configuration à trois places, un moteur V8 alimenté au méthanol développant plus de 2 500 chevaux combinés à 670 chevaux de moteurs électriques pour une puissance totale de plus de 3 000 chevaux, avec un accent sur un rapport d’appui aérodynamique de 4:59. et trois finitions différentes, chacune avec des designs de carrosserie uniques. Le rendu d’une voiture concept visible à côté de la Tachyon Speed originale est appelé « Tartarus », la variante utilisée dans Asphalt Legends Unite.  Les sections arrière de toutes les carrosseries de toutes les variantes étaient exposées.
Au MAX, il atteint une vitesse maximale d’environ 537,5 km/h, ce qui en fait le troisième véhicule le plus rapide du jeu asphalt 9, juste derrière le Koenigsegg Jesko Absolut et le Devel Sixteen. L’accélération au lancement et la maniabilité sont excellentes, mais l’efficacité du nitro est considérablement insuffisante. Malgré ses statistiques suggestives, le Tartarus est difficile à atteindre sa vitesse maximale supposée. Cela s’explique non seulement par son efficacité nitro abominable, mais aussi parce qu’au-delà de 300 km/h, son accélération diminue considérablement jusqu’à atteindre 450 km/h. Son incapacité à effectuer efficacement des 360 degrés ou des dérives de perforation limite encore davantage son potentiel. et il a une accélération pire à l’antenne, comme Devel Sixteen. Cependant, lorsqu’on utilise Nitro Shockwave, il a une accélération beaucoup plus lente en l’air que Explosive Nitro.

High detailed model created by SQUIR team.

Because different computers have different disks topology, it might be necessary to change the textures patches on the destination computer.
Thank you for buying SQUIR models

Retro Racing Wheels 80s – Type 2
A detailed set of non-branded retro racing wheels inspired by classic motorsport and aftermarket wheel designs of the 1980s and early 1990s. The model features a dense multi-spoke center, deep stepped rim, exposed hardware, center-lock style hub detail, valve stem, tire, and additional small mechanical elements for a more authentic period-correct appearance.
Designed as a generic wheel rather than a replica of any specific manufacturer or product, making it suitable for custom automotive projects, restomods, racing builds, period-correct vehicles, and retro-inspired renders.
The mesh is carefully modeled with clean topology and detailed geometry suitable for close-up renders while remaining practical for use in larger vehicle scenes.
Features: detailed multi-spoke wheel design, separate tire and wheel components, center-lock inspired hub assembly, exposed rim hardware, valve stem detail, clean polygon topology, UV mapped geometry, materials and textures, and a retro 1980s–1990s motorsport aesthetic.
Suitable for automotive visualization, vehicle customization, racing scenes, games, animations, and other CGI projects.

description_text:
La Lotus E-R9 est une étude de conception d’une voiture de course d’endurance électrique hypothétique qui doit débuter la course lors de la saison 2030.
Fini en noir et or éclatants – un clin d’œil évident à l’héritage pionnier de Lotus en sport automobile qui a conduit à 13 titres de champions de Formule 1 – le véhicule électrique présente une verrière élégante de type avion de chasse, montée au centre dans un tronc à aile delta. Les innovations incluent une aérodynamique active avancée avec des panneaux de carrosserie « morphing » et des surfaces de contrôle montées verticalement pour faciliter les virages à grande vitesse.
E-R signifie Endurance Racer, tandis que 9 est le numéro de compétition soigneusement choisi en hommage au passé de Lotus. C’est au volant d’une Lotus Mark IX que l’équipe de course a fait ses débuts aux 24 Heures du Mans, avec le fondateur de la société Colin Chapman parmi les pilotes en compétition. Nous étions en 1955, ce qui signifiait que le concept de voiture de course E-R9 – si elle était courue en 2030 – célébrerait le 75e anniversaire de la Mark IX.
Parmi les innovations aérodynamiques principales de la voiture, il y a ses panneaux de carrosserie en « transformation ». Située sur le profil delta-wing, cette adaptabilité – où les surfaces actives peuvent changer de forme et d’attitude face au flux d’air soit en appuyant sur un bouton du conducteur, soit automatiquement selon les entrées des capteurs de performance – offrirait un minimum de traînée sur les lignes droites et un maximum d’appui aérodynamique dans les virages.
Des surfaces de contrôle verticales à l’arrière généreraient des forces aérodynamiques pour aider la voiture à changer de direction, sans les limitations d’adhérence au niveau du contact avec le pneu. Le résultat est un jeu de course partiellement conduit comme une voiture et en partie piloté comme un avion de chasse.
La Lotus E-R9 est équipée d’une transmission électrique avancée alimentant chaque roue indépendamment, un système amélioré par le vectorisation du couple. Elle s’appuie sur une technologie déjà intégrée à la Lotus Evija purement électrique, bien que pour l’E-R9 elle soit entièrement réglable par le conducteur en déplacement.

description_text:
Highly detailed Rigged 3D model of the Nissan Skyline GT-R R32 (basic interior included), meticulously crafted to maintain exact real-world proportions and clean mesh/material organization. Produced by Anatolian Studios, this model is designed to be instantly ready for your renders, animations, or visualization projects without requiring any redesign, scaling, or adjustments.
Key Features:

  - 
Built to Real-World Scale: Modeled accurately in meters with exact physical proportions — no rescaling needed.

  - 
Detailed Exterior & Basic Interior: Fully detailed body, cabin, and trim, suitable for both close-up hero shots and animation.

  - 
Clean, Organized Structure: Every body panel, wheel, light, and trim piece is a separate, logically named object, grouped under Chassis / Exterior / Glass / Interior / Lights / Wheels, with materials named to match their parts for a fast, professional workflow.

  - 
Easy-to-Edit Materials: Clean Principled BSDF setup using solid-color materials, no advanced texturing or node knowledge required.

  - 
Correct Glass Setup: Transparent and glass surfaces are properly configured and export-friendly across all included formats.

  - 
Scene Ready: Centered at origin (0,0,0) with reset transforms and a single master parent, so the entire vehicle can be moved, rotated, or scaled as one unit.

Vehicle Rig (included):
The .blend file includes a production-ready vehicle rig, no add-ons needed. 
One slider steers both front wheels and the steering wheel together; drive the car forward and all four wheels roll automatically at the correct rate. Also included: per-axle and per-wheel manual spin, independent suspension travel on all four corners, and body pitch/roll for braking dive and cornering lean. Bones are cleanly named (CTRL_Root, CTRL_Body, CTRL_Wheel_FL/FR/RL/RR) with pivots centered on each axle, and the model is skinned so the skeleton carries over to the FBX and glTF files.
Documented rig guide (pdf) is included in the files.
Included File Formats:

  - 
.blend (Native Blender file — full rig with automatic steering and wheel roll, materials assigned, rendered in Cycles/Eevee)

  - 
.fbx (Widely supported format, retains geometry and material data)

  - 
.fbx (rigged) (Same model with bones and skinning included)

  - 
.obj & .mtl (Universal 3D format)

  - 
.gltf / .glb (Optimized format for real-time engines, web viewing, and AR/VR)

  - 
.glb (rigged) (Same model with bones and skinning included)

  - 
.usdz / .usdc (Universal Scene Description — AR Quick Look, iOS, and USD pipelines)

Technical Specifications:

  - 
Polygons: 250000

  - 
Vertices: 130000

  - 
Geometry: Tris

  - 
Textures: No

  - 
Materials: Yes

  - 
UV Mapped: Mixed

  - 
Rigged: Yes (.blend, .fbx, .glb)

Please Note:

  - The rigged and un-rigged versions are supplied as separate files. The standard .fbx / .glb / .obj / .usdz files contain no skeleton and keep the full group hierarchy intact; the files marked rigged contain the bones and skinning.

  - The rig's automatic steering and wheel roll are expression-driven and run in Blender. In FBX and glTF the bones, skinning and wheel pivots are fully present and can be posed or animated, but that automation does not transfer — a limitation of the interchange formats, not of the model.

Disclaimer: This is an unofficial, fan-made model created for visualization purposes and is not affiliated with or endorsed by the manufacturer. All brand names, logos, and trademarks are property of their respective owners.

Light Skipper: Team Red
The Light Skipper Space Racer is the perfect model to use for Sci-Fi themed races. With their pod styled design, rigged landing gear and cockpit, custom rigged pilot models, this model will be all you need to fill out your race tracks.
The Light Skipper Space Racer: Team Red is a highly detailed and feature rich 3D model, along with a matching rigged pilot model. All assets were made within Blender, with the exception of the decal images which were made using Affinity.
Included with the .blend file are 2K and 4K texture options (the 2K textures are applied to the exported models by default), and separate decal images with a stencil for making custom designs. Also included is a file of exported OBJ, FBX, and Glb models.All details and specifications can be found in the included guide.
The full Light Skipper collection is available to buy on my page. This includes all 6 Light Skipper variants along with a custom Light Skipper. La Czinger 21C (21C pour 21st Century) est une hypercar hybride conçue par le constructeur automobile américain Czinger, et produite à 80 exemplaires à partir de 2021. description_text:
Highly detailed Rigged 3D model of the Porsche 911 Dakar (interior included), meticulously crafted to maintain exact real-world proportions and clean mesh/material organization. Produced by Anatolian Studios, this model is designed to be instantly ready for your renders, animations, or visualization projects without requiring any redesign, scaling, or adjustments.
Key Features:

  - 
Built to Real-World Scale: Modeled accurately in meters with exact physical proportions — no rescaling needed.

  - 
Detailed Exterior & Interior: Fully detailed body, cabin, and trim, suitable for both close-up hero shots and animation.

  - 
Clean, Organized Structure: Every body panel, wheel, light, and trim piece is a separate, logically named object, grouped under Chassis / Exterior / Glass / Interior / Lights / Wheels, with materials named to match their parts for a fast, professional workflow.

  - 
Easy-to-Edit Materials: Clean Principled BSDF setup using solid-color materials, no advanced texturing or node knowledge required.

  - 
Correct Glass Setup: Transparent and glass surfaces are properly configured and export-friendly across all included formats.

  - 
Scene Ready: Centered at origin (0,0,0) with reset transforms and a single master parent, so the entire vehicle can be moved, rotated, or scaled as one unit.

Vehicle Rig (included):
The .blend file includes a production-ready vehicle rig, no add-ons needed. 
One slider steers both front wheels and the steering wheel together; drive the car forward and all four wheels roll automatically at the correct rate. Also included: per-axle and per-wheel manual spin, independent suspension travel on all four corners, and body pitch/roll for braking dive and cornering lean. Bones are cleanly named (CTRL_Root, CTRL_Body, CTRL_Wheel_FL/FR/RL/RR) with pivots centered on each axle, and the model is skinned so the skeleton carries over to the FBX and glTF files.
Documented rig guide (pdf) is included in the files.
Included File Formats:

  - 
.blend (Native Blender file — full rig with automatic steering and wheel roll, materials assigned, rendered in Cycles/Eevee)

  - 
.fbx (Widely supported format, retains geometry and material data)

  - 
.fbx (rigged) (Same model with bones and skinning included)

  - 
.obj & .mtl (Universal 3D format)

  - 
.gltf / .glb (Optimized format for real-time engines, web viewing, and AR/VR)

  - 
.glb (rigged) (Same model with bones and skinning included)

  - 
.usdz / .usdc (Universal Scene Description — AR Quick Look, iOS, and USD pipelines)

Technical Specifications:

  - 
Polygons: 595000

  - 
Vertices: 600000

  - 
Geometry: Quads

  - 
Textures: No

  - 
Materials: Yes

  - 
UV Mapped: Mixed

  - 
Rigged: Yes (.blend, .fbx, .glb)

Please Note:

  - The rigged and un-rigged versions are supplied as separate files. The standard .fbx / .glb / .obj / .usdz files contain no skeleton and keep the full group hierarchy intact; the files marked rigged contain the bones and skinning.

  - The rig's automatic steering and wheel roll are expression-driven and run in Blender. In FBX and glTF the bones, skinning and wheel pivots are fully present and can be posed or animated, but that automation does not transfer — a limitation of the interchange formats, not of the model.

description_text:
A fully modeled Volvo S90 executive sedan, built inside and out with a complete physically-based (PBR) material workflow. 
Every exterior panel, light, wheel, and interior component uses realBase Color, Metallic, Roughness, and Normal maps — nothing is flat-shaded or placeholder. The rear tail lamps use a true emissive shader for a genuine glowing-LED look, and every glass surface (windshield, side windows, headlight and taillight lenses) carries correct alpha transparency, so the car reads correctly the moment it's imported — no relinking textures or rebuilding materials required.
*Exterior*Full body shell with a glossy automotive paint finish
Complete glazing: windshield, rear window, side windows, headlight lenses, taillight lenses, and running-light covers, all with real transparencyDetailed front and rear light clusters, including glowing red LED tail-lamp strips
Chrome trim, window surrounds, and badge details (Volvo emblem, S90 script)
Full wheel assemblies — rims, tires, brake discs, and calipers
Exhaust tailpipes and underbody bumper/diffuser detail
Rear diffuser/trim accent piece at the bumper (separate object)
Door shut-lines, panel gaps, and body creases modeled for close-up realism
*Interior*Dashboard with instrument cluster, center infotainment screen, and a wood-tone trim insert across the dash and door caps
Front seats and rear bench, styled with a stitched, woven cloth-look upholstery pattern in a light cream/gray tone that contrasts with the black exteriorCenter console, steering wheel, and front/rear door trim panels
Speedometer/gauge cluster geometry
Cabin holds up under close interior camera angles — visible stitching, seat panel seams, and door-pillar trim
**Technical Specifications
**Objects   2 — main car body + rear bumper trim accent
Polygon count   1,820,956 tris total (1,805,389 body + 15,567 trim)
Vertex count    1,670,643
Materials   46 total (44 on the car body, 1 on the trim piece, 1 unused slot)
Texture maps    
Base Color
Metallic
Roughness,
Normal — 2048 × 2048 per material
Real-world scale    ~5.0 m (L) × 2.0 m (W) × 1.4 m (H) equivalent 
Texture count   166 image files
UV layout   Single UV channel per object, clean unwrap
Transparency    Real alpha-based glass on all glazing and light lenses
Emission    Dedicated emissive shader on tail-lamp LED elements
What's Included.blend — native Blender file FbxObjDaeTexture files 
Please NoteAll files are constantly updated, so once you have purchased them you have access to all improvements and updates that appear.

description_text:
Photorealistic, high-quality and accurate 3D model of 2027 Mercedes-Benz GLE Coupe with high detailed interior, openable hood and trunk. 
Main features:

  - Originally created with 3ds Max 2020 and rendered with Corona 12

  - Three MAX files with Corona, V-Ray and Standard 3ds Max materials. V-Ray scene, lighting and materials are similar to native Corona file

  - MAX, BLEND, C4D, MB, FBX and OBJ formats include two different file structures: default and detached, saved as separate files. Default file structure has objects being merged to larger instances (like body, doors, wheels, lights) and multi-materials assigned. Detached file structure offers more separate objects (up to 150-200 per model) and a single material per object assigned

  - Subdivision modifier is available in history for MAX, MB, C4D and BLEND files. You can get access to original non-smoothed mesh by deactivating the Subdivision modifier

  - Doors, trunk, hood, charging and fuel caps can be opened

  - Unit system is set to metric (millimeters). Real-world scale

  - All textures and materials are included and assigned

  - 34 textures, which vary in resolution from 33x796px to 8192x8192px

Special notes:
  - BLEND file has textures embedded. To unpack go to File -> External Resources -> Unpack Resources

description_text:
Highly detailed Rigged 3D model of the Porsche 911 Targa 4S (interior included), meticulously crafted to maintain exact real-world proportions and clean mesh/material organization. Produced by Anatolian Studios, this model is designed to be instantly ready for your renders, animations, or visualization projects without requiring any redesign, scaling, or adjustments.
Key Features:

  - 
Built to Real-World Scale: Modeled accurately in meters with exact physical proportions — no rescaling needed.

  - 
Detailed Exterior & Interior: Fully detailed body, cabin, and trim, suitable for both close-up hero shots and animation.

  - 
Clean, Organized Structure: Every body panel, wheel, light, and trim piece is a separate, logically named object, grouped under Chassis / Exterior / Glass / Interior / Lights / Wheels, with materials named to match their parts for a fast, professional workflow.

  - 
Easy-to-Edit Materials: Clean Principled BSDF setup using solid-color materials, no advanced texturing or node knowledge required.

  - 
Correct Glass Setup: Transparent and glass surfaces are properly configured and export-friendly across all included formats.

  - 
Scene Ready: Centered at origin (0,0,0) with reset transforms and a single master parent, so the entire vehicle can be moved, rotated, or scaled as one unit.

Vehicle Rig (included):
The .blend file includes a production-ready vehicle rig, no add-ons needed. 
One slider steers both front wheels and the steering wheel together; drive the car forward and all four wheels roll automatically at the correct rate. Also included: per-axle and per-wheel manual spin, independent suspension travel on all four corners, and body pitch/roll for braking dive and cornering lean. Bones are cleanly named (CTRL_Root, CTRL_Body, CTRL_Wheel_FL/FR/RL/RR) with pivots centered on each axle, and the model is skinned so the skeleton carries over to the FBX and glTF files.
Documented rig guide (pdf) is included in the files.
Included File Formats:

  - 
.blend (Native Blender file — full rig with automatic steering and wheel roll, materials assigned, rendered in Cycles/Eevee)

  - 
.fbx (Widely supported format, retains geometry and material data)

  - 
.fbx (rigged) (Same model with bones and skinning included)

  - 
.obj & .mtl (Universal 3D format)

  - 
.gltf / .glb (Optimized format for real-time engines, web viewing, and AR/VR)

  - 
.glb (rigged) (Same model with bones and skinning included)

  - 
.usdz / .usdc (Universal Scene Description — AR Quick Look, iOS, and USD pipelines)

Technical Specifications:

  - 
Polygons: 1970000

  - 
Vertices: 1950000

  - 
Geometry: Quads

  - 
Textures: No

  - 
Materials: Yes

  - 
UV Mapped: Mixed

  - 
Rigged: Yes (.blend, .fbx, .glb)

Please Note:

  - The rigged and un-rigged versions are supplied as separate files. The standard .fbx / .glb / .obj / .usdz files contain no skeleton and keep the full group hierarchy intact; the files marked rigged contain the bones and skinning.

  - The rig's automatic steering and wheel roll are expression-driven and run in Blender. In FBX and glTF the bones, skinning and wheel pivots are fully present and can be posed or animated, but that automation does not transfer — a limitation of the interchange formats, not of the model.

Disclaimer: This is an unofficial, fan-made model created for visualization purposes and is not affiliated with or endorsed by the manufacturer. All brand names, logos, and trademarks are property of their respective owners.

description_text:
Asset BreakdownThe Overall ConceptThis premium stylized vehicle asset is expertly engineered for futuristic racing titles, cyberpunk action games, seasonal event updates, street racing simulators, and digital marketplace listings. Representing a high-performance cyber SUV outfitted with an aggressive widebody aero kit and wrapped in a dark purple and neon-orange Jack-o'-Lantern Halloween livery, this model serves as an exceptional flagship player vehicle, high-speed boss ride, or dynamic seasonal event prop. It delivers a sleek, high-octane, and striking Halloween aesthetic while maintaining fully optimized topology for real-time engine performance.
Dark Purple Cyber Livery, Neon Orange Drips, and Jack-o'-Lantern GraphicsThe vehicle body features a vibrant, high-contrast material finish textured with professional-grade PBR shaders to capture satin body paint, emissive neon accents, and custom vinyl graphics. The exterior panels are clad in a deep metallic purple wrap featuring a fierce, glowing orange Jack-o'-Lantern grin along the side doors, complemented by vibrant orange flame-like splatter graphics along the hood, roof, and side skirts. Integrated orange LED strips trim the front splitters, air intakes, and side sills, accentuating its aggressive racing lines.
Opaque Dark Tinted Glass and Aggressive Racing StanceAdhering strictly to professional marketplace documentation standards, the windshield and side windows are modeled using solid, opaque, deep jet-black tinted glass geometry. This clever design layout completely eliminates the performance overhead associated with processing complex real-time glass refraction, cockpit interiors, or internal dashboard physics. The SUV features wide stance matte-black multi-spoke alloy wheels wrapped in low-profile performance tires, slotted brake discs, a massive rear GT wing spoiler, and sleek LED headlight strips.
Aggressive Widebody Cyber SUV SilhouetteThe asset assembly is characterized by its instantly recognizable, aerodynamic sports crossover proportions, featuring flared widebody fender arches, lowered stance, sharp front splitters, and a aggressive rear spoiler assembly. The design perfectly balances futuristic hypercar styling with iconic Halloween motifs. The asset is structured in the file seedream-4.0_A_futuristic_sporty_cyber_SUV_with_an_edgy_widebody_kit_customized_with_a_dark_p-0.jpg to present a clean, dynamic front three-quarter standing perspective view, maximizing presentation value and marketplace browser click-through rates.
Optimized Game-Ready GeometryBuilt specifically for seamless real-time engine implementation, the model features a highly optimized polygonal footprint. The mesh is logically constructed with clean, quad-dominant topology, keeping the poly-count low while maintaining razor-sharp edges on the aero splitters, widebody fenders, and smooth roof curves. This clean layout allows technical artists to easily assign distinct material IDs (for the metallic purple paint, emissive orange decals/LEDs, opaque black glass, and low-profile rubber tires) or effortlessly bake clean normal, roughness, metallic, and emissive maps in modern engines like Unreal Engine and Unity.
Technical NotesFiles Included: FBX, GLB, OBJ, STL, Optimized PBR Texture Maps (4K/2K) with Emissive Maps.
Game-Engine Ready: The main vehicle chassis, widebody aero kit, independent wheels, and rear wing assembly are organized in a clean hierarchy with a correct, center-grounded pivot point positioned at the base center of the footprint to ensure immediate, effortless setup of vehicle physics, lighting blueprints, or drivable actor blueprints.
Quick Tip: Maximize the neon Halloween vibe by enabling Bloom and Screen-Space Reflections in your engine's post-processing stack. Placing this vehicle on a wet asphalt street at night or on a glossy reflective showfloor will showcase the vibrant neon reflections and self-illuminating emissive maps along the chassis.

description_text:
An adjustable incline weight bench modelled at real-world scale, in the same fictional MORVEK line as our boxing bags. The frame is a black powder-coated steel structure (square and flat rectangular tubes) with a fine orange-peel finish, subtle edge wear and a white MORVEK wordmark printed on both sides of the main beam. The backrest pivots on a bolt through the rear upright and is held by a hinged round strut whose cross pin drops into one of six slots of the notched rack plates bolted to the rear post - the mechanism is built the way real benches work. Two black PU pads (leather grain, grey seam stitching under the rolled edge, debossed wordmark near the top of the backrest) sit on black ABS boards. Rubber end caps and plugs close every tube; two treaded transport wheels on bolted brackets behind the rear foot and a ribbed T handle on the front upright let the bench tip and roll. All hardware (hex bolts, nuts, strut pin) is zinc-plated.
Model

  - 4 separate, cleanly named objects: WB_Frame, WB_Pads, WB_Boards, WB_Rubber.

  - 6,508 faces / 11,036 triangles / 5,640 vertices, quads and triangles only, no n-gons, closed manifold parts.

  - Transforms applied, origin on the floor under the footprint centre, units in metres.

  - Non-overlapping UVs laid out proportionally (isotropic texels), one PBR material per object.

Textures (PNG, PBR metalness workflow, non-embedded, {Object}_{Type}.png)

  - Per object: BaseColor, Roughness, Metalness, AO, Normal (OpenGL + DirectX).

  - WB_Frame 4096 x 4096; WB_Pads 4096 x 4096; WB_Rubber 2048 x 2048; WB_Boards 1024 x 1024.

  - Zinc hardware and the worn edges are driven by the Metalness map.

Formats

  - FBX (binary), OBJ + MTL, glTF 2.0 (separate .bin + textures), Blender 5.2 (.blend with materials set up, relative texture paths).

  - Each format zipped with its texture set; previews rendered in Blender Cycles.

Notes

  - Overall 65 x 120 x 100.2 cm; seat pad 28 x 40 cm at 48 cm; backrest pad 30 x 86 cm, modelled at 40 degrees.

  - No plugins required. Lighting / HDRI not included. Fictional design and brand.

description_text:
Highly detailed Rigged 3D model of the Porsche 356 C (basic interior included), meticulously crafted to maintain exact real-world proportions and clean mesh/material organization. Produced by Anatolian Studios, this model is designed to be instantly ready for your renders, animations, or visualization projects without requiring any redesign, scaling, or adjustments.
Key Features:

  - 
Built to Real-World Scale: Modeled accurately in meters with exact physical proportions — no rescaling needed.

  - 
Detailed Exterior & Basic Interior: Fully detailed body, cabin, and trim, suitable for both close-up hero shots and animation.

  - 
Clean, Organized Structure: Every body panel, wheel, light, and trim piece is a separate, logically named object, grouped under Chassis / Exterior / Glass / Interior / Lights / Wheels, with materials named to match their parts for a fast, professional workflow.

  - 
Easy-to-Edit Materials: Clean Principled BSDF setup using solid-color materials, no advanced texturing or node knowledge required.

  - 
Correct Glass Setup: Transparent and glass surfaces are properly configured and export-friendly across all included formats.

  - 
Scene Ready: Centered at origin (0,0,0) with reset transforms and a single master parent, so the entire vehicle can be moved, rotated, or scaled as one unit.

Vehicle Rig (included):
The .blend file includes a production-ready vehicle rig, no add-ons needed. 
One slider steers both front wheels and the steering wheel together; drive the car forward and all four wheels roll automatically at the correct rate. Also included: per-axle and per-wheel manual spin, independent suspension travel on all four corners, and body pitch/roll for braking dive and cornering lean. Bones are cleanly named (CTRL_Root, CTRL_Body, CTRL_Wheel_FL/FR/RL/RR) with pivots centered on each axle, and the model is skinned so the skeleton carries over to the FBX and glTF files.
Documented rig guide (pdf) is included in the files.
Included File Formats:

  - 
.blend (Native Blender file — full rig with automatic steering and wheel roll, materials assigned, rendered in Cycles/Eevee)

  - 
.fbx (Widely supported format, retains geometry and material data)

  - 
.fbx (rigged) (Same model with bones and skinning included)

  - 
.obj & .mtl (Universal 3D format)

  - 
.gltf / .glb (Optimized format for real-time engines, web viewing, and AR/VR)

  - 
.glb (rigged) (Same model with bones and skinning included)

  - 
.usdz / .usdc (Universal Scene Description — AR Quick Look, iOS, and USD pipelines)

Technical Specifications:

  - 
Polygons: 90000

  - 
Vertices: 95000

  - 
Geometry: Quads

  - 
Textures: No

  - 
Materials: Yes

  - 
UV Mapped: Mixed

  - 
Rigged: Yes (.blend, .fbx, .glb)

Please Note:

  - The rigged and un-rigged versions are supplied as separate files. The standard .fbx / .glb / .obj / .usdz files contain no skeleton and keep the full group hierarchy intact; the files marked rigged contain the bones and skinning.

  - The rig's automatic steering and wheel roll are expression-driven and run in Blender. In FBX and glTF the bones, skinning and wheel pivots are fully present and can be posed or animated, but that automation does not transfer — a limitation of the interchange formats, not of the model.

This asset is a premium high-quality static model designed specifically as a fixed, non-animated prop suitable for static rendering, concept art visualization, set dressing, apocalyptic survival games, and digital marketplaces. The surface materials expertly simulate weathered steel and rusted automotive body panels across the distressed orange and blue body, with rough metallic corrosion defining the damaged hood, rusted bumpers, and tall tailfin supports. Dirty rubber and mud textures cover the off-road tires, while dark tinted glass finishes the windshield and side windows, complemented by a weathered metallic shader on the grille, bumper guards, and trim. This meticulous material setup allows the model to catch bright studio lighting cleanly while casting a soft shadow on the isolated white background. This premium high-quality static model is perfectly suited for static game environments, post-apocalyptic wasteland dioramas, survival game asset libraries, or gritty cinematic props.

description_text:
A modern heavy bag modelled at real-world scale and textured as a new product: black semi-gloss PU body with a fine leather grain, double contrast stitching at the panel seams, a red band with a fictional wordmark front and back, and a stitched reinforcement disc on the top. Four nylon webbing straps (woven texture, box-X stitching) are sewn on stitched PU backing patches that wrap over the top rim; each strap loop closes around a D-ring bar with a PU keeper sleeve. Four chains of 13 interlocking links run to a central ring, followed by a swivel with eye bolts and a classic spring snap hook (riveted gate). A bottom D-ring hangs from a flat sewn webbing loop.
Model

  - 5 separate, cleanly named objects: HB_Bag, HB_Straps (4 straps + 4 patches + 4 keepers + bottom loop), HB_Rings (4 D-rings, bottom D-ring, central ring), HB_Chains (52 links), HB_Swivel (swivel, eye bolts, snap hook).

  - 16,636 faces / 32,896 triangles / 16,480 vertices, quads and triangles only, no n-gons, every part closed.

  - All hardware is physically linked: links pass through each other, the D-ring bars sit in the strap folds, the eye bolts go through the ring and the hook, with sub-millimetre bites at the contacts (no floating parts).

  - Transforms applied, origin at the lowest point (bottom ring), centred on the hanging axis, units in metres.

  - Non-overlapping UVs (one pelt per revolved part, strips for the straps and chain links), one PBR material per object.

Textures (PNG, PBR metalness workflow, non-embedded, {Object}_{Type}.png)

  - Per object: BaseColor, Roughness, Metalness, AO, Normal (OpenGL + DirectX).

  - HB_Bag 4096 x 4096; HB_Straps, HB_Rings, HB_Chains, HB_Swivel 2048 x 2048.

Formats

  - FBX (binary), OBJ + MTL, glTF 2.0 (separate .bin + textures), Blender 5.2 (.blend with materials set up, relative texture paths).

  - Each format zipped with its texture set; previews rendered in Blender Cycles.

Notes

  - The bag hangs 1.86 m from the hook top to the bottom ring; the bag body is 110 x 35 cm.

  - No plugins required. Lighting / HDRI / ceiling mount not included. Fictional design and brand.

  - Same fictional MORVEK line as our free-standing punching bag and weight bench.
